articles.title: Night of the Coyotes review – border-crossing role-play is tourist attraction in struggling Mexican town
articles.summary: Clara Trischler’s absorbing feature sees residents of the small town of El Alberto hired to play characters in a re-enactment of the migrant experience. In contrast to other migration documentaries, which focus on the new life that awaits those who have crossed the border, Clara Trischler’s…
body: This terrifying sequence of events is later revealed to be make-believe. In the small Mexican town of El Alberto, whose population has been depleted by a steady flow of migration to the US, role-playing re-enactments function as both a means of deterrent and, oddly enough, a tourist attraction. Advertised as Caminata Nocturna – “night hike” in Spanish – these events recruit local residents to perform as specific characters, including the fearsome “coyotes”, AKA human traffickers. The attendees experience the full scale of a border-crossing operation, from being loaded on vans to intimidation from their coyotes, and police interrogation.

articles.title: Premature review – sunny charm provides screwball energy for surprise-pregnancy comedy
articles.summary: First-time director Kevin Walls creates a film sweet-natured enough to cancel out some comedy misfires as flatmates Eilidh and Cameron prepare for parenthood. The pram in the hallway is the enemy of good art, or so the famous quote goes.
body: Elle Watson is artist Eilidh, who works as a barista in a museum cafe. She has a friends-with-benefits setup with her flatmate Cameron (James Rottger); he has a job in finance and, after two degrees, a mountain of student debt and years in a mind-numbing entry-level position, he’s finally lined up an interview for his dream job. It would be crazy to have the baby, but Eilidh doesn’t take the abortion tablets. She can’t give Cameron a coherent reason why not; fair enough, it’s her decision, a gut feeling. Walls sensibly doesn’t go anywhere near the pro-choice/anti-abortion debate.

But it is a shame his script seems to naturally click more with Cameron’s point of view as he agonises about how a baby will impact his career. Eilidh cheerfully breezes through pregnancy – though inexplicably she turns mumzilla in one scene, demanding that Cameron help her break into a house to steal a secondhand cot, wearing tights over their heads. It’s a scene that reduces the film’s IQ and likability by about 10%. Elsewhere, there are some moments of gentleness, like Cameron’s lovely dad and his no-nonsense wisdom. “Life doesn’t give two shits about your plans, son.”

articles.summary: Acclaimed Catalan filmmaker Carlos Marques-Marcet (“10,000 km,” TIFF Platform winner “They Will Be Dust”), with his first showrunning gig, and sisters Mireia and Joana Vilapuig (“Selftape”) will rub shoulders with creators from Galicia, Finland, Iceland, Latvia, Mexico and Portugal at the second…
body: On the heels of last year’s flawless launch of Mind the Gap, set up to boost top-tier series in their financial stage of financing, more than double the number of projects from a bigger geographical spread were submitted this year.
Out of the 11 selected titles, eight came from open calls, and three were invited by European industry partners Seriencamp, ECAM Forum and Iberseries.

“It’s been more challenging for our selection committee but also extremely exciting,” said Victor Sala, Serielizados Pro honcho who welcomed new collaborations with the Baltics, through Latvia’s entry “The Man Behind a Mask,” and the sustained ‘love affair’ between Finland and Spain.

“Apart from Spain – obviously!, we received the largest number of projects from Finland – five or six”, said the industry chief who picked with his team the Finnish ‘crime “Bloodwine” from Helsinki-filmi (“The Summer Book,” “Codename-Annika”) and psycho drama “Dangerous Woman” from Gutsy Pictures (“L/Over”). Sala also underscored Helsinki-based Tekele’s involvement in the Spanish dramedy “Not Girls”, first original series produced by top Catalan banner Fasten Films (“The End of It”).

articles.title: Finland’s Gutsy Pictures Pacts With MTV, Germany’s Zeitsprung, Sweden’s Götafilm on Zaida Bergroth’s ‘Dangerous Woman’ (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: Value-driven Finnish outfit Gutsy Pictures headed by Marika Makaroff (“Moominvalley,” “L/Over”) has secured a greenlight from MTV Finland and added co-producers Zeitsprung in Germany and Götafilm in Sweden for the psycho-thriller “Dangerous Woman.” Already pre-bought by TV4 in Sweden, the…
body: “I’ve wanted to tell this story for 10 years, but when I first wrote it, the idea felt almost too extreme,” Makaroff said, before adding: “Today, hatred has become increasingly normalized, and I wanted to explore what happens when it moves beyond words and becomes physical.”

Makaroff, who opened up about her own experience of abuse while promoting “L/Over” in 2025, said she’s approached the character of Laura in “Dangerous Woman” “with compassion”. “She [Laura] has spent a lifetime being belittled, dominated and abused, and eventually reaches her breaking point. Through her, I’m asking a difficult question: can violence or revenge ever be justified? And if we become those we hate, who does that serve?”
“The series is a mix of dark humor, psychological thriller and social drama, but ultimately it is a story about humanity, grace and forgiveness,” she observed.

articles.title: ‘Practical Magic 2’ Casts a Spell Over U.K., Ireland Box Office as Oasis Doc Rocks No. 2
articles.summary: Warner Bros.’ “Practical Magic 2” cast a winning spell over the U.K. and Ireland box office, dethroning “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” after a six-week reign to claim the top spot with an opening weekend of £2.7 million ($3.7 million).
body: Sony’s superhero juggernaut “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” moved to fifth position in its seventh frame, generating $1.1,illion. The blockbuster’s running total reached $132.7 million, overtaking “Spider-Man: No Way Home,” “Avatar,” and “No Time to Die” to claim the No. 3 spot on the all-time U.K. and Ireland box office chart, trailing only “Star Wars: The Force Awakens” and “Skyfall.”

Signature Entertainment’s survival sequel “Fall 2” opened in sixth place with $648,421. “Insidious: Out of the Further,” distributed by Sony, followed in seventh position in its fourth week, adding $619,084 to raise its running total to $9.9 million.

Entertainment Film Distributors’ action thriller “Runner,” starring Alan Ritchson and Owen Wilson, bowed in eighth place with $517,727. Paramount landed the ninth spot with the 45th anniversary 4K re-issue of “Raiders of the Lost Ark,” which grossed $326,263. Altitude Film Distribution’s “Coyote vs. Acme” rounded out the top 10 in its fourth frame, collecting $188,463 to push its cume to $2.6 million.

articles.title: Kore-eda Hirokazu to Receive Cinema Honorary Award From Singapore Film Festival, Yim Soon-rye to Head Asian Competition Jury
articles.summary: The Singapore International Film Festival (SGIFF) will honor Japanese filmmaker Kore-eda Hirokazu with its Cinema Honorary Award and has named Korean director Yim Soon-rye jury head of its Asian Feature Film Competition. The 37th edition of SGIFF runs Oct. 21 to Nov. 1.
body: “Look Back” marks the first live-action feature adaptation of any manga by Fujimoto Tatsuki. The film follows Fujino, an elementary school student whose confidence as her class’s star cartoonist is upended when a reclusive classmate, Kyomoto, proves to be a far superior artist. Their rivalry curdles into obsession, and even after the two eventually connect and forge a friendship through their shared pursuit of manga, an opportunity to create a serial later arrives and pulls them apart. The film competed for the Golden Lion at the Venice Film Festival.

Yim, who studied filmmaking at the University of Paris 8, debuted with “Three Friends” in 1996 and went on to direct “Waikiki Brothers,” the box office hit “Forever the Moment,” “The Whistleblower,” “Little Forest” and “The Point Men.” She has also spent 12 years as president of an animal rights association and co-leads the Korean Center for Gender Equality in Film. Yim will speak at SGIFF Industry Days on Oct. 27.

articles.title: Memorable moments from the Emmys and everything you couldn't see on TV
articles.summary: Backstage, the winners continued the celebrations off-screen and addressed some of the ceremony's most viral moments.
body: Welsh actor Matthew Rhys and US actress Jean Smart made Emmy Awards history during TV's biggest night in Hollywood this year, which brought out stars from the small screen, film, sport and music.

Hosted by Law & Order SVU star Mariska Hargitay - the first woman to host in 15 years - the ceremony was packed with cameos from celebrities, emotional speeches, touching tributes and plenty of banter.

The cast and crew behind Apple TV's sleeper hit celebrated the supernatural TV comedy's popular first season, which nabbed six wins on Monday and another eight at the Creative Arts Emmys earlier this month.

Asked about the show being relatively smaller and unknown to some audiences, the cast and creators reflected backstage with gratitude for the grassroots efforts to promote the show through word-of-mouth early on.

articles.title: Jeremy Thomas obituary
articles.summary: Film producer who enjoyed his greatest success with the 1987 epic The Last Emperor for which he won an Oscar. Asked whether he had ever cautioned restraint from a director, the film producer Jeremy Thomas replied: “My nature would be to go further and see what we can get away with.” Thomas, who has…
body: Thomas, who has died aged 77, was an expert in getting away with it. A taste for irreverence ran in his family: he was the son of Ralph Thomas, director of the Doctor … comedies that began in 1954 with Doctor in the House, and the nephew of Gerald Thomas, who made all 31 Carry On titles. Jeremy’s own films, however, were risky rather than risque.

Bad Timing (1980), the first of three collaborations with the director Nicolas Roeg, explored a destructive love affair blighted by jealousy, attempted suicide and rape. Rank, the studio behind it, withheld from the start of the print its familiar company ident showing a man striking a gong. According to Thomas, the studio also denounced the picture as “a sick film made by sick people for sick people”.

He teamed up on several occasions with David Cronenberg, first for an adaptation of William S Burroughs’s Naked Lunch (1991), featuring a sentient, fleshy typewriter that talks through its anus, and most infamously for a film of Crash (1996), JG Ballard’s novel about a group of outsiders who get their sexual kicks from car accidents.

articles.title: Welsh actor Matthew Rhys makes Emmy Awards history with double win
articles.summary: He becomes the first person to win two lead acting prizes in one night at the prestigious TV ceremony.
body: Welsh actor Matthew Rhys has made history at the Emmy Awards, becoming the first person to win two lead acting prizes in one night.
Rhys was recognised at the prestigious US ceremony for his roles in supernatural TV comedy Widow's Bay and psychological thriller The Beast In Me.
On stage, Rhys dedicated his second award "to the great and good people of Wales, who were as much a nurture as anyone else".
"We are a small but mighty nation. This is incredible," he said, adding "Diolch yn fawr iawn" - which means "thank you very much" in Welsh.
